size_policy.label: existing 80-line checker policy for listed legacy contract types; configurable, not an approved one-screen definition

parser_limits.markdown_links: literal inline links plus one-line full, collapsed, and defined shortcut reference links; duplicate and explicit unresolved references are uncheckable
parser_limits.wikilinks: file targets only; headings and blocks are removed before resolution
parser_limits.paths: inline code and plain text; a path needs a start of ~/ ./ ../ or /, a folder before the name, a trailing slash, or a known file ending; inline code with a slash and no such signal counts only when it is on disk; a plain name with no folder is not read as a path; text in angle brackets is a placeholder and is not checked
parser_limits.commands: inline code with a dollar-space prompt, or with a flag, placeholder, quoted value, or script path after a lowercase first word; a plain line that starts with Run and names a command; single-line commands in sh, bash, zsh, and shell fences; the whole executable name is checked, dots included; dynamic, builtin, and control syntax is not checked and never evaluated
parser_limits.skills: dollar-prefixed and slash-prefixed names, and exact stale names in inline code; other bare inline names are not checked
parser_limits.banned_words: whole words, any letter case, on every line outside a code fence, quotation marks included; one exception: inside double quotes after a banned_word_prohibition_cues phrase on the same line
parser_limits.absent_paths: inline-code paths listed right after an absent_path_cues phrase must stay absent; a path in backticks that is missing on a line under a declared_absent_headings section may be absent; links, imports, and scripts there are always checked
parser_limits.instructions: a sentence that holds an instruction_verbs word and no checked form is counted per file as an unchecked instruction; it is never a finding
parser_limits.approvals: coverage requires an explicit read-only binding of contract path, SHA-256, and approval identifier
